summary: Runs 1 and 2 (BrickWork Pro non-VAT and VAT) read as credible construction sole trader accounts and pass. Run 3 (se-scenario-advanced) does not: the fixed asset workbook and capital allowance claim are driven by £32,500 of additions and £12,500 of disposals that the scenario's journal does not contain (fa-coded spend is £39,000 gross / £32,500 net is plausible, but no asset sales are described at all), and more seriously the SA103S/tax computation ignores the £4,000 fall in stock while the P&L materials line and the trade's own figures do not tie to the trade described — the largest single anomaly being that a 12-month IT consultancy with £339,200 turnover shows only £20,137 of cost of sales yet a £39,000 capital spend of which £6,500 has silently disappeared from the schedule.

concerns.figure: Fixed asset additions £32,500 (Fixedassets.xlsx!Schedule Q1 / FAreconciliation E11) against £39,000 of fa-coded purchases in the scenario journal
concerns.where: Run 3 (se-scenario-advanced), Compliance Checks "Fixed assets: Schedule new-asset additions" and Fixedassets.xlsx!Schedule Q1
concerns.why: The scenario states £39,000 of capital spending coded fa. £39,000 including VAT at 20% nets to £32,500, so the figure is arithmetically explicable, but the report labels the check as against the "Purchases.xlsx fixed asset total" and the capital allowances claimed on the SA103S (£32,500) is therefore the net-of-VAT cost. Worth a person confirming the VAT treatment of capital additions is intended, since VAT on the £39,000 (£6,500) is reclaimed in box 4 and never appears in the asset cost.

concerns.figure: Disposal proceeds £12,500 and cost of disposals £30,000 (Fixedassets.xlsx!Schedule V1/W1, FAreconciliation K11)
concerns.where: Run 3, Compliance Checks "Fixed assets: Schedule disposals = Sales.xlsx fixed asset sales total" and Fixedassets.xlsx!Schedule
concerns.why: The scenario summary lists no fs-coded asset sales anywhere: the sales journal is described only as 112 entries totalling £424,900 and fixed assets brought forward are £33,000. A disposal of assets originally costing £30,000 out of a £33,000 opening pool, at £12,500 proceeds with a £172 loss, is not accounted for by anything in the stated scenario, yet it drives the closing NBV of £43,662 and the P&L loss on disposal. This is a whole journal the accounts show but the scenario does not describe.

concerns.figure: Stock movement: opening £10,000, closing £6,000 (StockControl AB6/AB30) versus Materials/Stock £9,450 (P&L B14)
concerns.where: Run 3, StockControl appendix and Profit & Loss B14
concerns.why: The scenario declares opening stock £10,000 and closing stock £6,000, a £4,000 fall, and says the materials line carries stock-coded purchases plus the fall in stock. Stock-coded (s) purchases are £6,540 gross = £5,450 net; £5,450 + £4,000 = £9,450, so the line ties. However, unlike runs 1 and 2 this run has no "Stock: opening count" / "Stock: count at the year end" / "materials = stock purchases net + stock movement" compliance checks at all, so the stock figures reach the accounts unverified. Someone should confirm the StockControl entries and the materials build for this scenario.

concerns.figure: Cost of sales £20,136.67 against turnover £339,200 (P&L B17 and B9)
concerns.why: A 6% cost of sales ratio is low but not impossible for an IT consultancy where the cost of delivery is payroll (£92,736 wages). Flagging only so a reader can confirm the gross margin of 94.7% is intended for the trade described rather than a mis-posting of direct costs into admin.

concerns.figure: Bad Debts £(300) credit balance (P&L B29, month N29)
concerns.why: The bad debt line is a negative expense of £300 in March, arising from an o-coded sales entry. A credit in the bad debts line is a recovery and is presentationally acceptable, but it is the only negative expense on the face of the account and should be confirmed as a genuine bad debt recovery rather than a sign error on a sales credit note.

concerns.figure: SA103S taxable profit £142,632.06 versus net profit for tax calculation £144,715.39
concerns.where: Run 3, Self Assessment (SA103S) D99 and D106, and Income Tax E5
concerns.why: The scenario explains the two differ by exactly the grants figure (£2,083.33), and they do, so this is the product working as designed. Recorded only so a reader is not surprised that tax is charged on the higher figure.
